answer: The trellis multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and falcon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4067 identities would post 1394 proofs and burn roughly 3 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
